Growth retardation. As discussed on p.1798 gonadorelin an- alogues have been given with growth hormone to short girls without growth hormone deficiency, in an attempt to delay pu- berty and bone maturation and thus maximise the final height achieved. Use in growth hormone-deficient children has also been investigated. However, there is some doubt about the extent of benefit, and in any case the concept of such treatment in chil- dren who are not clinically deficient in growth hormone is con- troversial, and some authorities do not consider it appropriate.
